text: Carpentry involves shaping and connecting wood to build structures like houses, cabinetry, and furnishings. The work relies on numerous methods, specifically the formation of joints that link separate timber sections. Connections range from basic butt joints, which simply abut two pieces, to intricate mortise and tenon designs intended to increase stability and strength. After assembling these links, wood components are aligned and finished with varnish. This coating shields the material from damage while adding a shiny surface. Ultimately, carpentry turns timber into durable, aesthetic objects that often survive for many generations.
